title: Hotel Marketing Data: What to Track Each Month
excerpt: The few numbers a resort or hotel needs each month: bookings and cost per booking by channel, OTA commission as acquisition cost, lead time, length of stay, and a report template.
description: Hotel marketing data to track monthly: cost per booking by channel, OTA commission, lead time, length of stay, with a one-page report template.
html:
To run hotel marketing on data, track five things every month: bookings and room revenue by channel, the cost of each booking by channel (with OTA commission counted as an acquisition cost), booking lead time, average length of stay, and enquiry-to-booking rate. GA4 and your booking engine supply most of it.

Start with the question, not the dashboard

Most small resorts and hotels either track nothing or have three dashboards nobody opens. The useful middle ground is a short list of numbers that answer one question: where should next month's marketing time and money go?

That question breaks down into a few smaller ones. Which channels bring bookings? What does each booking cost to win? How far ahead do guests book, and for how long? Where do people drop off before booking? If a number does not help answer one of these, leave it out of the monthly report.

Where the data comes from

Your booking engine or PMS

This is the source of truth for bookings: dates, room type, rate, source, booking date and stay dates. Most booking engines and property management systems used in India can export a monthly report to a spreadsheet. Check that each booking carries a source (direct website, MakeMyTrip, Booking.com, walk-in, phone, WhatsApp, travel agent). If staff enter phone and WhatsApp bookings without a source, fix that first, because those are often your cheapest bookings and they disappear from the picture.

GA4 on your website

Google Analytics 4 tells you how people reached your site and what they did there. For a resort, set up a few key events: clicks on "Book now" or "Check availability", booking engine starts, completed bookings (if your engine can pass them back), WhatsApp button clicks, call clicks and enquiry form submissions. Use UTM tags on links from Instagram bio, WhatsApp broadcasts and email so they do not all show up as "direct".

Channel dashboards

OTA extranets show views, conversion and ranking signals for your listing. Google Business Profile shows calls, direction requests and website clicks. Google Ads and Meta show spend and clicks. You do not need to copy everything across; pull the two or three numbers that feed your monthly sheet. Our analytics and reporting page explains how we set these up.

Cost per booking by channel

This is the number that changes decisions. For every channel, divide what it cost you by the bookings it brought.

  • OTAs: commission paid on the month's stays, plus any promotion or visibility programme fees.
  • Google Ads and metasearch: ad spend, plus booking engine fees on those bookings.
  • Meta ads: ad spend, divided by bookings you can trace to enquiries from those ads.
  • Direct and repeat: payment gateway fees and any staff time you choose to count.

An example, with illustrative numbers. Say a room night sells for ₹6,000 and the average stay is two nights, so a booking is worth ₹12,000. If an OTA charges 18 percent commission on that, the booking costs ₹2,160 to acquire. If your brand-search ads cost ₹9,000 in a month and brought six direct bookings, each cost ₹1,500. Neither number is good or bad on its own; the point is to compare them side by side.

Treat OTA commission as marketing spend

Many owners put commission under "deductions" and ad spend under "marketing", which makes OTAs look free and ads look expensive. Put both in the same column. Once you do, decisions become clearer: perhaps spending a little more on brand-name search, or on a reason to book direct, is cheaper than the commission it replaces. Equally, you may find an OTA brings guests at a fair cost in the off season that you could not reach any other way. The tactics for shifting that mix are in the post on increasing direct bookings.

Lead time and length of stay

Lead time is the number of days between booking and check-in. A resort near Bengaluru may see many bookings made within a week of a long weekend, while a destination wedding venue in Udaipur may see bookings months ahead. Lead time tells you when to run promotions: there is little point advertising Diwali packages three days before the holiday if most guests booked a month earlier.

Length of stay tells you which offers to build. If most direct guests stay one night but OTA guests stay two, look at what the OTA listing shows that your site does not. If weekday stays are short, a "stay three, pay two" weekday offer might be worth testing.

Look at both by channel and by season. Monsoon in Kerala and peak winter in Rishikesh behave differently, and averages across the whole year hide that.

A monthly report template

One page, filled in on the first working day of each month. Copy this into a spreadsheet.

Below the table, add four lines: website sessions, booking engine starts, completed direct bookings, and enquiries received on WhatsApp and phone. Then write two sentences: what changed since last month, and what you will do differently next month.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Counting enquiries as bookings. Track both, separately.
  • Comparing a busy month with a quiet one. Compare with the same month last year where you can.
  • Ignoring cancellations. Record bookings net of cancellations, or add a column for them.
  • Letting "direct" swallow everything. Without UTM tags and source fields, you cannot tell Instagram from repeat guests.
  • Reporting without a decision. Every monthly report should end with one change to make.

Once tracking is in place, it also tells you which pages on your site need work; the booking engine conversion guide covers what to do when engine starts are high but completed bookings are low.

Frequently asked questions

Can GA4 track bookings made in a third-party booking engine?

Often, yes, but it depends on the engine. Some booking engines support adding your GA4 measurement ID or Google Tag Manager so that completed bookings are recorded as events. Others run on a separate domain and need cross-domain tracking. Ask your provider exactly what they support, then make a test booking and check that it appears in GA4 before relying on the numbers.

Is OTA commission really a marketing cost?

For decision-making, it is useful to treat it that way. Commission is what you pay the OTA to bring you a guest, which is the same job ads do. Putting both in one column lets you compare cost per booking honestly. It does not mean OTAs are bad value; in some seasons and for some guests, they may be your cheapest way to fill a room.

What is a good booking lead time for a resort?

There is no universal good number. Lead time depends on your location, guest type and season. Weekend getaway properties close to cities usually see short lead times, while destination weddings and long holidays book far ahead. What matters is knowing your own pattern by channel and season so you time promotions and rate changes before guests make their decisions.

How often should a small hotel review its marketing data?

Monthly is enough for most small and mid-sized properties. A one-page report on the first working day of the month, with bookings, revenue and cost by channel, keeps decisions grounded without becoming a chore. Check ad spend weekly if you are running paid campaigns, so that a broken landing page or runaway budget does not go unnoticed for a full month.

Where to start

Export last month's bookings from your booking engine and add a source to every row, including phone and WhatsApp bookings. Fill in the template above with what you have, even if some cells are blank. Then add UTM tags to your Instagram bio and WhatsApp links so next month's report is more complete.
